purpose: Transform character emotional state, knowledge, beliefs, objectives and relationships into a controlled perception model that determines what each character attends to, notices, interprets, ignores and experiences within the same canonical scene reality.
core_principle: One canonical reality can produce multiple valid character perceptions because attention and interpretation are constrained by state.
perception_model: reality → sensory access → attention → salience → interpretation → emotional coloration → perceived meaning → intention
director_rules: Maintain one canonical scene reality; never create contradictory physical realities merely to satisfy POV.
Perception must be explainable from knowledge, emotion, objective and sensory access.
Characters notice what is relevant to their current objective before neutral background detail.
Emotional state can amplify or suppress salience but cannot manufacture impossible evidence.
Belief influences interpretation, not objective physical facts.
A character may misread an objectively visible action.
A character may overlook a visible detail when attention is occupied elsewhere.
Different characters may assign different meanings to the same event.
Perception must distinguish observed fact from interpretation.
Unknown information remains outside perception unless acquired through a valid scene event.
The audience may receive controlled information outside any single character's perception only when explicitly authorized by the audience model.

output_schema.canonical_reality: scene facts shared across all perspectives
output_schema.blind_spot_map: relevant details not perceived or not recognized
output_schema.other_character_read: perceived intention of other active characters with confidence
output_schema.validation: reality, access, knowledge, emotion, interpretation, chronology and audience-boundary checks

pass_conditions: every major perception has a causal basis
